title: How to spot a malicious link without clicking it
description: You can inspect a link safely before it ever loads. Hover, read the real domain, spot lookalikes, and ignore the padlock myth.

scenes.big: Check the link before you click it
scenes.say: You can check a link without ever clicking it. Here's how.
First, hover over it. On a phone, press and hold. The real address appears. Read the part just before the first single slash. In this fake, the real site is login-check dot xyz, not the bank.
Watch for lookalikes, like a number one in place of the letter L, and unfamiliar endings. Short links hide where they lead, so expand them with a link checker first.
And don't trust the padlock. A scam site can use HTTPS too. It only means the connection is encrypted, not that the site is honest.

steps: Read the domain before the first /
scenes.say: Still unsure? Don't click. Open the site yourself, or forward the email to report at phishing dot gov dot UK. Follow for more tiny habits that stop big attacks.
